expectations.text: The response identifies that python datetime values are bound as TIMESTAMP and compared to a DATE column, so Oracle applies INTERNAL_FUNCTION to the column and cannot use IDX_ORDERS_DATE
expectations.evidence: 'python-oracledb sends your datetime values as TIMESTAMP binds, but orders.order_date is a DATE... It converts the column to TIMESTAMP... the B-tree on plain order_date can't be used as an access predicate.'

expectations.text: The response fixes it by binding as DATE (e.g. cursor.setinputsizes(start_ts=oracledb.DB_TYPE_DATE, ...)) or by CAST(:start_ts AS DATE) / TO_DATE on the parameter side
The response says rebuilding the index will not help
expectations.evidence: 'Rebuilding the index: nothing is wrong with the index... A rebuild changes nothing.'

expectations.text: The response says a hint is not the right fix (or not needed once the bind type is fixed)
expectations.evidence: '/*+ INDEX(orders IDX_ORDERS_DATE) */: ... The best the hint can give you is an INDEX FULL SCAN ... It also hides the real bug'.

expectations.text: The response explains why the SQL Developer test with literal dates uses the index (the literals are DATE, so no conversion)
expectations.evidence: 'SQL Developer uses the index because DATE '2026-11-23' and TO_DATE(...) literals are of type DATE. Types match, so there's no conversion'.

expectations.text: The response gives verification with DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY_CURSOR and says what to expect: INDEX RANGE SCAN with access(...) predicates and peeked binds of type DATE
expectations.evidence: DISPLAY_CURSOR('&sql_id', NULL, 'ALLSTATS LAST +PEEKED_BINDS'); expects '(DATE)', 'INDEX RANGE SCAN IDX_ORDERS_DATE', 'access("ORDER_DATE">=:START_TS AND "ORDER_DATE"<:END_TS)'.

expectations.text: The response does not recommend creating a new index as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: Explicitly rejects function-based index ('Don't'); covering index only 'if the query is still too slow after the fix'.

expectations.text: Each reported issue carries an explicit severity label (e.g. High / Medium / Low, or Critical / Major / Minor); ordering alone does not count
expectations.evidence: No explicit severity labels; issues are given as prose/numbered explanations.

overall_notes: none. Minor: does not mention ALLSTATS LAST requires gather_plan_statistics/statistics_level=ALL to populate A-Rows.
